_note: Every value the source does not state comes from one of these rules (or a cited span). A rule says what it sets, the value, and why. Changing a value here changes every practice that uses it on the next build; the practice records rule ids, not copies.

pace-guide.sets: seconds per in/out breath when the text gives no timing
pace-guide.cite: engine/compile.mjs natural-phase default pace [5, 6]; the same pace as the existing Ajahn Lee Method 2 demo
pace-guide.note: A visual guide only. Narration says once to breathe at your own pace; the orb is not a command.

moment-one-breath.sets: length of 'a moment' at a base
moment-one-breath.note: one full breath: long enough to arrive, short enough not to dwell

traverse-with-breath.sets: how back-and-forth attention moves are paced

value.per_round_trip: one breath: out to the further spot on the in-breath, back on the out-breath

traverse-with-breath.note: the text ties the moves to no breath phase; pairing them gives the visual a clock. Users can ignore the breath link.

count-by-analogy.sets: a repetition count the text leaves open between parallel steps

value.from: the count of the immediately preceding parallel steps

count-by-analogy.note: Method 1 gives 'seven times' for Bases 1–2 and 2–3 and no count for 3–4

stillness-rounds.sets: breaths in the stillness stage (no length in the text: 'when you've reached this level of stillness')
stillness-rounds.note: the user's rounds control (+/−) changes it

feel-breaths.sets: breaths of plain breath-feeling before the bases

spread-breaths.sets: breaths for 'let the refined breath … spread to the lower parts of the body'

whole-body-breaths.sets: breaths in the closing whole-body stage

attention-at-nostrils.sets: where attention is drawn while counting
attention-at-nostrils.cite: method-1:p3.s3 (focused on the breath as it comes in and out of the nostrils)

posture-accessibility.note: the text gives half-lotus; we name it and allow any steady upright seat so the practice is usable on a chair

recollection-optional.sets: whether the devotional opening can be skipped
recollection-optional.note: kept by default (it is the text's first step); skippable for users who prefer a secular session

condition-dropped.sets: use of a line outside the condition the text attaches to it
condition-dropped.note: the line is used for the breath sensation alone, without the light sign it follows in the text; flagged on every use

caution-cross-method.sets: applying a caution from one chapter to another
caution-cross-method.note: same author and book; the head bases are spots above the base of the throat

no-nimitta-scripting.note: signs are conditional on the meditator's experience; the session never asks anyone to see lights. Responses live in the Ask layer with the source's own handling.

narration-margin.sets: minimum silence after a narration line before the next line or phase-locked cue
narration-margin.note: the voice never runs into the next instruction; long lines must be split or given another breath

editorial-facet.sets: discovery facets (aim, method) not stated as such in the text
editorial-facet.note: chosen by us from the content for filtering; never shown as the teacher's claim

eyes-closed-default.sets: eyes, when the text is silent
eyes-closed-default.note: Thai forest default; the dark player view assumes it

guidance-breaths.sets: breaths given to narrated guidance inside a breathing stage
guidance-breaths.note: each scripted modifier (caution, image, widen…) gets one breath of its own so lines never stack; adds to the stage length

fit-narration.note: seconds = max(min_s, measured narration + pause + margin); before TTS an estimate at 2.3 words/s

lead-in.sets: silence + bowl before the first word
lead-in.note: PRACTICE-MEDIA: session start = singing bowl strike with a long tail; the voice waits for the attack to settle

stage-chime.note: PRACTICE-MEDIA 'round end: tiny chime', used for stage changes so the ear can follow the structure with eyes closed

sweep-one-breath.sets: breaths for one 'let the breath sensation spread / flow from A to B' sweep
sweep-one-breath.note: in-breath at the starting spot, out-breath carries it to the far end: one sweep per breath, as traverse-with-breath

step-breaths.sets: breaths given to each step of a stepwise breath practice whose text sets no length (e.g. the sixteen steps of MN 118)
step-breaths.note: long enough for one step to be noticed, short enough that the whole sequence fits a sitting; the session-length picker adds open time at the end, never more steps

explore-breaths.sets: breaths for an open-ended exploring instruction with no length ('observe…', 'adjust it until…', 'learn four ways…')
explore-breaths.note: a few breaths of exploring; the narration never names a number

phrase-breaths.sets: breaths of silence after each wish or phrase in a recited reflection (goodwill)
phrase-breaths.note: the phrase is heard, then two breaths to let it sink in

open-sitting.sets: time added at the end of a practice when the user picks a session longer than the practice as written
open-sitting.note: the player never invents more steps: extra minutes are silent sitting with the last stage (or more stillness rounds where the practice has them)

cite-only-source.sets: how a practice cites a text whose translation may not be quoted (all rights reserved)
cite-only-source.note: instructions are our own words; each one names the verse(s) it rests on and links the translation; no quote is stored or shown

resting-base-default.sets: the spot the picture shows when the text says to rest on 'whichever base seems most comfortable'
resting-base-default.note: the meditator chooses; the picture shows the lowest base on the list, the one the headache caution never excludes. Narration never names it

non-body-step-visual.sets: what the picture shows for a step whose object is not a body place (feelings, the mind, mental qualities)
non-body-step-visual.note: feelings are shown as the whole body softly lit; the mind and mental qualities as the light widened around the body (space). The picture is a support, not a claim about where these are

first-tetrad-beginner.sets: the beginner form of a sixteen-step practice
first-tetrad-beginner.cite: MN 118 note 2 (p44.s4): the fourth step refers to the fourth jhāna; the later tetrads build on a settled body-tetrad
first-tetrad-beginner.note: beginners get the first tetrad and open time; the full form keeps all sixteen steps
